newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to hand down 1998/99 budget on May 12.
newsitem.headline: Australia to hand down 1998/99 budget on May 12.

text.p: Australian acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer said on Tuesday the government would announce the budget for the 1998/99 fiscal year ending June 30 on May 12 next year, marking a return to surplus for government finances.

"The federal government ... will towards the end of the (1997/98) financial year see a budget brought down on May 12, 1998, which will have a surplus for the first time in many years," he told reporters.
The Liberal-National government has forecast an underlying surplus -- excluding windfalls such as asset sales -- of A$1.6 billion for the fiscal year to June 30, 1999.
In its 1997/98 budget on May 13 this year, the government projected an underlying deficit of A$3.9 billion.
The 1997/98 headline budget outcome is expected to be a surplus of A$6.4 billion but the government has set the underlying budget performance as its chief fiscal measure
Australia's underlying budget was last in surplus -- A$402 million -- in 1990/91.
